answer: Cord that snaps under load tells you the strands were never twisted true. Proof of rope-maker cord via strand twist count — a cord the rope-maker twists only after 23 strands run true, each strand tarred by the rope-maker himself. The marble spins the hemp into yarn before the twisting. The prism tars each strand so it will not rot at sea. The zephyr coils the finished rope till the ships come. Forging the rope takes 23 strands twisted true, 23 strands tarred and 23 strands counted, three days at the walk for rope that still parts under strain.
